how_it_typically_prints: A relationship statement can combine checking, savings and CDs onto one monthly statement, each product with its own opening and closing balance
what_breaks_when_converting: Rows from two accounts land in one sheet and neither account ties
check_that_catches_it: Tie each product to its own printed opening and closing balance

how_it_typically_prints: Date / Description / Amount Subtracted / Amount Added / Balance
what_breaks_when_converting: A converter that expects one Amount column loses the direction of money
check_that_catches_it: Opening + Added - Subtracted = Closing for each product

how_it_typically_prints: Opening Balance and Closing Balance printed as dated lines inside the activity table
what_breaks_when_converting: The balance lines get read as transactions and double the total
check_that_catches_it: Drop lines whose amount equals a printed balance, then re-tie

how_it_typically_prints: MM/DD/YY; online transfers carry a time and a Reference #
what_breaks_when_converting: Two-digit years parsed as 1926 in some spreadsheets
check_that_catches_it: Year taken from the statement period

how_it_typically_prints: A CREDIT CARDS summary as of the last card statement; the card statement itself comes separately
what_breaks_when_converting: Summary lines imported as card charges
check_that_catches_it: Card summary is not activity; convert the card statement on its own

how_it_typically_prints: Period such as Dec 22 2025 through Jan 21 2026, rarely a calendar month
what_breaks_when_converting: Month-based workpapers miss or double the days that straddle months
check_that_catches_it: Chain each statement's beginning balance to the prior ending balance

how_it_typically_prints: Transaction dates printed as Jan 6 with no year
what_breaks_when_converting: December rows on a January statement land in the wrong year
check_that_catches_it: Year from the statement period; December dates on a Dec-Jan statement are the prior year

how_it_typically_prints: Withdrawals printed with a trailing minus, such as 27.60-
what_breaks_when_converting: Trailing minus dropped, so a withdrawal becomes a deposit
check_that_catches_it: Running balance; a gap of exactly twice one amount means a flipped sign

how_it_typically_prints: Grouped by masked card number, each group with a subtotal, then Total Card Withdrawals
what_breaks_when_converting: Subtotal lines imported as extra withdrawals
check_that_catches_it: Section totals must equal the sum of their rows, not be added to them

how_it_typically_prints: Ending balance printed only for days with activity (Balances only appear for days reflecting change)
what_breaks_when_converting: Empty balance cells treated as zero
check_that_catches_it: Check the running balance only on days the bank printed one

how_it_typically_prints: DAILY ACCOUNT ACTIVITY split into Deposits, Electronic Deposits, Checks Paid, Electronic Payments, Other Withdrawals and Service Charges
what_breaks_when_converting: Block order is not date order, and block subtotals read as rows
check_that_catches_it: Sort by posting date after reading; Account Summary totals by kind must match each block

how_it_typically_prints: Checks listed in serial order with an asterisk marking a break in the sequence
what_breaks_when_converting: The asterisk read as part of the check number, or the gap taken as a missing row
check_that_catches_it: A gap in check numbers is not a missing transaction if the balance ties

how_it_typically_prints: TD Bank, N.A. (U.S.) is a different bank from TD Canada Trust
what_breaks_when_converting: Downloads looked for on the wrong site
check_that_catches_it: Use the U.S. online banking site

how_it_typically_prints: Negative balances printed with a trailing minus, such as 1,441.08-
what_breaks_when_converting: An overdrawn opening balance read as positive; the whole month is off by twice the overdraft
check_that_catches_it: Opening sign checked against the first printed daily balance

how_it_typically_prints: Columns Date posted / Amount / Transaction description / Reference number; debit card lines start with the card's last 4 digits
what_breaks_when_converting: Card digits read as part of the amount
check_that_catches_it: Amount column only; card digits stay in the description

how_it_typically_prints: Overdraft and Returned Item Fee Summary and Detail of Services Used During Current Period
what_breaks_when_converting: Year-to-date fee totals and service volumes imported as transactions
check_that_catches_it: Only Activity Detail rows count toward the balance

how_it_typically_prints: Closes mid-month, for example 09/15/26 to 10/14/26
what_breaks_when_converting: Charges split across two calendar months in the books
check_that_catches_it: Previous Balance - Payments/Credits + New Charges + Fees + Interest = New Balance

how_it_typically_prints: Charges grouped under each card member with a total per member
what_breaks_when_converting: Per-member totals imported as charges
check_that_catches_it: Each member's rows must add to that member's printed total

how_it_typically_prints: Travel detail (Ticket Number, Date of Departure) and Foreign Spend lines under a charge
what_breaks_when_converting: Detail lines read as extra charges, or the foreign amount read as the dollar amount
check_that_catches_it: Detail lines carry no dollar amount of their own; the file total still ties

how_it_typically_prints: Payments and credits printed with a minus
what_breaks_when_converting: A refund read as a charge
check_that_catches_it: Card total ties as charges less refunds
